title: Hardcoded Environmental Assumptions (Brittle Context)
pattern: Tests that assume specific local directory paths, exact clock dates, local time zones, or local system permissions.
why_bad: Tests fail immediately when run on other team members' machines, in continuous integration pipelines, or inside sandboxed build engines [178].
detection: Hardcoded absolute file paths, system usernames, or machine IP addresses in test bodies [269].
counterexample: Relative paths constructed dynamically using build environment variables: `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`.
fix: Use virtual resources, mock system clocks, relative paths, or environment variables to inject context dynamically during test execution [269].
source:
*   *The Pragmatic Programmer*, "Unreliable things" (p. 269) [269, 572]
*   *Software Engineering at Google*, "Hermetic Tests" (p. 218) [507]
